## Why these two sessions

The two sessions are one task split at the approval gate, so they are submitted together as one
transcript. Together they show the supervised pipeline: plan with traceability and a test strategy,
two plan rejections, the lead's decisions and approval before any code, a build that the lead rejected
twice on safety grounds, verification that caught a vacuous test, and an architecture revision driven by
the plan review (REQ-IX-ARCH-001 narrowed for v1, PR #31).

## Export notes

- Exported with `opencode export <sessionID>` and converted to markdown. Every message, tool call,
  tool input, and tool output appears in its original order and is otherwise unedited. Long tool
  outputs are folded in `<details>` blocks; nothing is truncated.
- Omitted as non-content: OpenCode step markers (`step-start` / `step-finish`, token counts) and file
  snapshot hashes; changed files of each step are listed instead. No model reasoning blocks were
  present in the export.
- Redacted: 0 occurrence(s) of credentials or the operator's email. Both exports were scanned
  for the course API key, `sk-` keys, Bearer tokens, and the email before conversion.
- The human messages were drafted with the help of a separate reviewing agent (Claude Code), then
  reviewed and sent by the lead; that work is recorded in the lead's AI-use log entries.
- Annotations after each human message were drafted by that reviewing agent from the session record at
  the operator's request and are **pending the operator's review**. A reason is given only where the
  operator stated one in the message. 12 human messages, 12 annotated.

```
@Prompt.md Follow this prompt.
Role: plan
Task: Plan one end-to-end slice that makes the AI install-risk advisory work in the running app against the course DeepSeek service: network-settings card group with user controls and first-use endpoint/key setup, dialog-flow wiring through policy and ApprovalCoordinator, a real InstallationGateway, and review UI in both Material 3 and Miuix dialogs.
Related IDs: REQ-IX-FR-001, FR-002, FR-003, FR-005, FR-006, FR-007, FR-008, FR-011, REQ-IX-ARCH-001, ARCH-002, REQ-IX-INV-001, INV-002, INV-004, INV-006, INV-007, REQ-IX-SEC-004, SEC-005, REQ-IX-MOD-001, ADR-001, ADR-002.2, ADR-002.4, ADR-002.5, ADR-002.6
Approved inputs: docs/plans/2026-11-21-approval-coordinator-binding-gateway.md (section 9 follow-up steps 3-5; approved, merged in PR #27); docs/plans/2026-11-20-autodialog-install-evidence.md; docs/plans/2026-11-21-autodialog-model-egress.md

Facts to verify and build on:
- No production code calls RequestInstallRiskAssessmentUseCase, DeterministicPolicyEngine, or ApprovalCoordinator today; installs go through the original InstallerX path.
- The current provider setup is a test configuration: GroqAiModelClient (BASE_URL https://api.groq.com/openai/v1), DEFAULT_MODEL_ID qwen/qwen3-32b, API key from System.getenv("GROQ_API_KEY"), which is never set for an Android app process. The transport is already OpenAI-compatible (OpenAiCompatibleTransport, response_format json_object, max_tokens 512).
- Production target is the course service: OpenAI-compatible base URL https://llm.cs.cityu.edu.hk/v1, model CS5351/DeepSeek-V4-Flash.
- ModelRequestGate reads current consent through a coroutine-context element; AutoDialogInstallEvidenceMapper already maps PackageAnalysisResult to InstallEvidence.
- Approval state stays in memory (persistence deferred, DEBT-003). Robolectric cannot run (BUG-003), so there are no JVM UI tests.

Scope (no exemptions; both theme families):
1. Settings: a new "AI install-risk advisor" card group on the network settings page in both NetworkPage.kt (Material 3) and MiuixNetworkPage.kt, with: an advisor on/off switch (default off), a consent switch for sending derived, non-identifying evidence (default off, with a short explanation), an endpoint/key configuration entry, and a read-only model/prompt version line. When allowInternetAccess is off, the advisor controls are disabled and no request is sent.
2. Provider, endpoint, and API key (decided by the lead):
   - Switch the production provider from the Groq test setup to the course service. Generalize the Groq-specific client into a provider-neutral OpenAI-compatible client behind the existing adapter interface (MOD-001); keep the advisor and policy unaware of the provider.
   - The first time the user turns the advisor on, require them to configure the endpoint and API key before it can be enabled. Prefill the endpoint with https://llm.cs.cityu.edu.hk/v1; the key is always user-entered. Cancelling leaves the switch off. Both can be edited later from the same card group.
   - Store both in app-private storage only. Never in BuildConfig, resources, assets, or any file packaged in the APK, so no key ships with the app. Exclude them from backup and from the app's settings export/import. Mask the key in the UI, and never log it or put it in audit, transcripts, or error messages. A missing key or endpoint disables the live call and never weakens a deterministic check.
   - Endpoint validation: HTTPS only, a well-formed URL. State how the existing egress allowlist and HttpProfile handling change so that only the configured host is reachable, and that requests still go through AiNetworkGate.
   - Model change: CS5351/DeepSeek-V4-Flash replaces qwen/qwen3-32b. This requires a new prompts/prompt_v1.1.yaml with a new prompt_version, matching PROMPT_VERSION and model id in code, and a passing prompt-sync check and semantic evaluation gate. Do not edit prompt_v1.0.yaml; mark it superseded.
   - Compatibility risks to resolve in the plan: whether the course gateway accepts response_format json_object, and whether the model emits reasoning text or uses up max_tokens 512 before the JSON. Propose request and validator handling and a fallback if json_object is rejected; the validator stays strict (no lenient parsing of free text into advice).
   - Live verification: replace GroqLiveAdvisorTest with a provider-neutral live test reading the key from an environment variable (propose the name, e.g. CS5351_LLM_API_KEY) and skipping without it. The matching change to .github/workflows/ci.yml (secret name in the semantic_eval job) is listed as a separate item for my approval. Never commit a key.
3. Entry wiring in the dialog flow: after analysis, map evidence, run the advisor only if switch, configuration, and consent are all present (the consent switch is the ModelRequestGate source), run DeterministicPolicyEngine, and route through ApprovalCoordinator. Advisor off, unconfigured, consent off, or model failure must still produce a deterministic decision (INV-004, INV-006). Read the requirements to decide which install modes are in scope, and state explicitly what happens in the notification and automatic-install flows; do not assume the dialog behaviour carries over.
4. A real InstallationGateway that wraps the existing install path at the S3 seam named in the approved plan; the coordinator is its only caller (ARCH-001). Register coordinator, in-memory store, ledger, and gateway in DI.
5. Dialog UI in both families: an advisory card (success likelihood, security risk, reasons, "advisory only" label, and failure/unavailable/unconfigured states) plus the policy decision. BLOCK disables install with the reason shown; REQUIRE_REVIEW needs an explicit Continue or Cancel; EXECUTE_ONCE proceeds. Strings in resources, following the existing translations pattern.

Plan requirements:
- Read the relevant existing files before proposing changes (network pages and view models, AppSettingsRepository and its storage, backup and settings export rules, InstallerViewModel, ProgressHandler, InstallerStage, both installer dialog families, AiModule, GroqAiModelClient, OpenAiCompatibleTransport, OkHttpAiTransport and the egress allowlist, AiRequestBuilder, prompts/prompt_v1.0.yaml, .github/scripts/course_gates.py prompt-sync).
- Split the work into build checkpoints, each of which compiles and passes tests: (0) provider generalization, prompt v1.1, and a live smoke call to the course endpoint run by me with my key (go/no-go for the rest); (A) settings, first-use setup, and key/endpoint storage; (B) gateway and DI; (C) ViewModel wiring; (D) Material 3 UI; (E) Miuix UI.
- List the tests first with IDs and requirement links: JVM unit tests for provider request/response handling against recorded course-style replies, key/endpoint validation and storage rules (not in export, masked), settings-to-gate logic, view-model and state mapping, and decision-to-UI-state mapping, plus ChokePointTest, prompt-sync, and the existing AI suites still passing. Also a manual device demo checklist (first-use setup and cancel, advisor off, consent off, internet off, LOW, HIGH, BLOCK, and model failure) as UI evidence.
- Identify any change to docs/architecture (for example ADR-002.2, ADR-002.4, ADR-002.5) as a human task; do not edit it.
- Include risks and an open-questions list. Stop after writing the plan and wait for my explicit approval.
```

```
351:     reason: Raw device capability list; only the derived abi_compatibility result is sent.
352:   - id: native_library_abis
353:     egress: local
354:     reason: Detailed APK capability data; aggregate signals are sufficient for advice.
355:   - id: authorizer_capability_raw
356:     egress: local
357:     reason: Backend identity and capability detail stay local; only an enum is sent.
358:   consent:
359:     requirement: REQ-IX-FR-011
360:     fields_shown: outbound_metadata_allowlist.fields
361:     prerequisites:
362:     - explicit_consent
363:     - network_enabled
364:     declined_or_withdrawn:
365:       model_calls: 0
366:       auto_approval: false
367:       decision: REQUIRE_REVIEW
368:       hard_block_precedence: true
369:       audit_events:
370:       - CONSENT_DECLINED
371:       - CONSENT_WITHDRAWN
372:   local_approval_binding:
373:     requirement: REQ-IX-INV-003
374:     retains:
375:     - target_package_name
376:     - operation_id
377:     - attempt_id
378:     - apk_sha256
379:     - target_user_id
380:     - install_mode
381:     - installation_backend
382:     - config_snapshot
383:     - policy_version
384:     note: Removing a field from outbound egress does not remove it from local approval binding or audit. The target package name stays local for binding and audit.
385:   negative_fit_criteria:
386:   - id: NFC-OUT-001
387:     criterion: With consent granted, after allowlisted free-text fields are sanitized and redacted, the complete outbound model request, including all metadata and the fully assembled
388:       prompt and messages, contains zero occurrences of the target package name, source package name, APK SHA-256, any signer SHA-256 value, source UID, sourceDir, label, installer or
389:       requester package identifiers, or any other field listed as local-only.
390:   - id: NFC-OUT-002
391:     criterion: The evidence leaf paths in the outbound request are exactly the allowlisted paths; every required field is present, and no additional evidence field appears at any nesting
392:       level.
393:   - id: NFC-OUT-003
394:     criterion: When consent is declined or withdrawn, model-call count is 0, auto-approval is false, the decision is REQUIRE_REVIEW, and any active hard prohibition remains BLOCK.
395:   - id: NFC-OUT-004
396:     criterion: 'Using a fixture whose target package name and install-source package name are distinct, independently of outbound egress: with the approval binding unchanged, revalidation
397:       succeeds and execution is permitted only through that valid local binding; then modifying only the bound target package name in the stored approval causes revalidation to fail,
398:       invalidates the prior approval, and results in zero backend submissions. The distinct source package name must not be mistaken for the bound target package.'
399:   - id: NFC-OUT-005
400:     criterion: After a configured cap truncates any allowlisted field, the evidence is not COMPLETE; the decision is REQUIRE_REVIEW with RECOLLECT, model calls are 0, and no auto-approval
401:       occurs.
402:   - id: NFC-OUT-006
403:     criterion: With consent granted, the complete outbound request contains no raw device API level, ABI list, native-library ABI list, authorizer package identifier, or other local-only
404:       compatibility fact; only the derived compatibility signals appear.
405:   approved_decisions:
406:   - id: PMA-OUT-001
407:     decision: Keep the target APK package name local in v1.
408:     scope: Applies only to the target APK package name within the v1 scope defined by REQ-IX-SCOPE-001.
409:     does_not_cover:
410:     - install_source_package_name
411:     - apk_sha256
412:     - signer_sha256_set
413:     - source_uid
414:     - other_outbound_allowlist_items
415:     status: approved
416:     approved_by: Member A
417:     confirmed_by: Member B
418:     rationale: The target package name remains available for local approval binding and audit and is not sent to the model in v1.
419:   pending_member_a_review:
420:   - id: PMA-OUT-002
421:     proposal: Keep the install-source package name and source UID local; send only package_source and source_confidence.
422:     rationale: Raw source identity can fingerprint the installer or device; categories preserve decision value.
423:   - id: PMA-OUT-003
424:     proposal: Keep raw APK and signer hashes, certificate details, and installed-app hashes local.
425:     rationale: The model cannot validate them; deterministic code and audit use them for binding, identity, and tamper checks.
426:   - id: PMA-OUT-004
427:     proposal: Include has_shared_uid and is_xposed_module as booleans while omitting raw sharedUserId and module details.
428:     rationale: Preserves structural risk signals without exposing identifiers.
429:   - id: PMA-OUT-005
430:     proposal: Use this allowlist as the single source for FR-002 collection review, FR-003 egress, FR-011 consent display, and SEC-004 validation.
431:     rationale: Prevents collection, consent UI, request builder, and tests from drifting apart.
432:   - id: PMA-OUT-006
433:     proposal: Cap declared_permissions at 200 entries and version_name at 256 characters before transmission.
434:     rationale: Bounds request size; the exact caps require Member A review.
435:   completeness:
436:     required_fields_always_present: true
437:     unknown_encoding: Required means the key is present. For unknown enum values use the documented unknown category; for other unknown values use JSON null. A missing binding field
438:       prevents dispatch. A missing required payload key fails validation.
439:     truncated_is_complete: false
440:     states:
441:     - COMPLETE
442:     - KEY_UNKNOWN
443:     - TRUNCATED
444:     - CONTRADICTORY
445:     - UNREADABLE
446:   derived_compatibility_signals:
447:   - platform_compatibility
448:   - abi_compatibility
449:   - storage_sufficient
450:   - install_relation
451:   - apk_identity
452:   - installer_capability
453: requirements:
454: - id: REQ-IX-FR-001
455:   type: functional
456:   priority: Must
457:   title: Accept approval request
458:   statement: When AI approval is enabled and an in-scope path is supported (InstallerActivity with InstallMode.AutoDialog or AutoNotification, Authorizer.None), the system shall create
459:     a unique installation operation ID for each single-APK request and an attempt ID for each model-analysis attempt, and shall start approval before any installation backend is invoked.
460:     AutoNotification shall complete assessment and decision before submission.
461:   fit_criterion: Submitting a supported APK produces a queryable operation ID; attempts are counted separately from provider dispatches; while approval is incomplete, installation-backend
462:     invocations are 0; a user retry keeps the operation ID unchanged and adds only an attempt ID; an out-of-scope path makes 0 model calls.
463:   source: V0.2 §5.1
464:   depends_on: []
465:   status: conceptual
466:   asr: false
467:   enforcing_component: ApprovalCoordinator
468:   verification:
469:     method: integration + negative
470:     test: 'planned: ApprovalRequestTest'
471:     evidence: planned
472:   source_links:
473:   - https://github.com/wxxsfxyzm/InstallerX-Revived/blob/main/app/src/main/java/com/rosan/installer/ui/page/main/installer/InstallerViewModel.kt
474: - id: REQ-IX-FR-002
475:   type: functional
476:   priority: Must
477:   title: Collect installation evidence
478:   statement: 'The system shall collect, locally, APK SHA-256, package name, version, declared permissions, signature-check result, installed-app signature comparison result, source information,
479:     target user, install mode, a configuration snapshot that affects installation, and compatibility facts needed for a local assessment: device API level, supported and required ABIs,
480:     native-library ABIs, minSdk and targetSdk, available storage, relevant platform restrictions, authorizer capability, and the installed-version relationship. Each evidence field records
481:     whether it is present, whether its value is known, and whether it is complete. Undetermined values shall be UNKNOWN and shall not be inferred. A truncated list, string, or compatibility
482:     fact is not complete. Target and source package names, raw hashes, source UID, signer material, paths, and raw device identifiers remain local.'
483:   fit_criterion: Fixed APK fixtures produce the expected evidence values; a missing source is UNKNOWN and does not by itself make the evidence KEY_UNKNOWN; a missing or unverifiable
484:     INV-003 binding field produces KEY_UNKNOWN. A permission list or version label that loses content at the configured cap is marked TRUNCATED and is not COMPLETE. A fixture with an
485:     unsupported ABI or a device API below minSdk produces a local INCOMPATIBLE assessment; missing device facts produce UNKNOWN. Contradictory local facts produce CONTRADICTORY. No outbound
486:     field is implied by collection alone.
487:   source: V0.2 §4.2
488:   depends_on:
489:   - REQ-IX-FR-001
490:   status: conceptual
491:   asr: false
492:   enforcing_component: InstallEvidenceCollector
493:   verification:
494:     method: unit + fixture
495:     test: 'planned: EvidenceCollectorTest'
496:     evidence: planned
497:   note: A missing source is recorded as UNKNOWN and is not by itself KEY_UNKNOWN; KEY_UNKNOWN applies only when a field bound by INV-003 is missing or unverifiable. Collection is local;
498:     egress is governed separately by SEC-004 and outbound_metadata_allowlist.
499:   completeness:
500:     required_fields_always_present: true
501:     unknown_encoding: Required means the key is present. For unknown enum values use the documented unknown category; for other unknown values use JSON null. A missing binding field
502:       prevents dispatch. A missing required payload key fails validation.
503:     truncated_is_complete: false
504:     states:
505:     - COMPLETE
506:     - KEY_UNKNOWN
507:     - TRUNCATED
508:     - CONTRADICTORY
509:     - UNREADABLE
510:   source_links:
511:   - https://github.com/wxxsfxyzm/CS5351-Project/blob/fcdd2348/app/src/main/java/com/rosan/installer/data/session/handler/ProgressHandler.kt#L51
512: - id: REQ-IX-FR-003
513:   type: functional
514:   priority: Must
515:   title: Real model analysis
516:   statement: After explicit outbound consent and when the network switch permits, and only for an in-scope path, the system shall send only the fields enumerated in outbound_metadata_allowlist
517:     to a real model service and obtain a structured advisory recommendation containing model identifier, prompt version, install_success_likelihood, security_risk, reasons, and evidence
518:     references. install_success_likelihood shall be HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, or UNKNOWN; security_risk shall be LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, or UNKNOWN. The recommendation is an estimate, not a guarantee,
519:     and shall not include installation or approval actions. Compatibility facts sent to the model shall be derived signals only. Each attempt shall make at most one provider dispatch
520:     and shall not retry automatically. Consent declined or withdrawn, network disabled, shall produce zero dispatches and no AI auto-approval; out-of-scope paths retain baseline behavior;
521:     hard prohibitions remain BLOCK.
522:   fit_criterion: An online integration returns model identifier, prompt version, both dimensions, and a contract-conforming recommendation; offline tests use fixed responses. Consent
523:     declined or withdrawn produces zero model calls and REQUIRE_REVIEW; network disabled produces zero model calls; an out-of-scope path produces zero model calls. A timeout produces
524:     no second automatic call. The outbound request contains only allowlisted leaf paths, including only derived compatibility signals, and contains no target package name, source package
525:     name, raw hash, signer hash, source UID, sourceDir, label, or raw device identifier. A response that states a guarantee or an installation action is INVALID.
526:   source: V0.2 §5.1
527:   depends_on:
528:   - REQ-IX-FR-002
529:   - REQ-IX-FR-011
530:   - REQ-IX-SEC-004
531:   status: conceptual
532:   asr: false
533:   enforcing_component: AIRiskAdvisor
534:   verification:
535:     method: integration (online) + offline fixed response
536:     test: 'planned: AdvisorIntegrationTest'
537:     evidence: planned
538:   note: Target and source package names, raw hashes, and identifiers stay local under outbound_metadata_allowlist.
539: - id: REQ-IX-FR-004
540:   type: functional
541:   priority: Must
542:   title: Validate model output
543:   statement: The system shall validate the model response's structure, required fields, enums, lengths, and evidence references. It shall require both install_success_likelihood and
544:     security_risk, reject unknown action fields, installation or approval instructions, guarantee language, fabricated evidence references, out-of-range content, and oversized output,
545:     and mark the response INVALID. An INVALID response shall not produce auto-approval.
546:   fit_criterion: Invalid JSON, a missing dimension, an illegal success-likelihood or risk enum, an unknown action field, an installation or approval instruction, a guarantee claim, an
547:     oversized response, and a fabricated evidence reference are each classified INVALID and produce no auto-approval. A response with both dimensions and valid references is accepted
548:     only after structural validation. Compatibility evidence references must resolve to transmitted allowlisted fields; local-only references in an outbound claim are rejected.
549:   source: V0.2 §4.2
550:   depends_on:
551:   - REQ-IX-FR-003
552:   status: conceptual
553:   asr: false
554:   enforcing_component: AIOutputValidator
555:   verification:
556:     method: unit negative
557:     test: 'planned: OutputValidationTest'
558:     evidence: planned
559: - id: REQ-IX-FR-005
560:   type: functional
561:   priority: Must
562:   title: Compute approval decision
563:   statement: The system shall determine ALLOW_AUTO, REQUIRE_REVIEW, or BLOCK from the effective policy version, evidence completeness, the local compatibility assessment, the validated
564:     install_success_likelihood and security_risk, and the human approval state, returning the DR rule ID and reason. Only an active deterministic hard prohibition may produce BLOCK;
565:     AI advice and human confirmation shall not override it. Favorable automatic continuation requires COMPLETE evidence, COMPATIBLE local compatibility, install_success_likelihood HIGH,
566:     security_risk LOW, and AUTO_RULES_MET. Any unfavorable or uncertain dimension, compatibility UNKNOWN or INCOMPATIBLE, evidence RECOLLECT, AI failure, consent denial, or token-budget
567:     failure produces REQUIRE_REVIEW. A first Continue in AWAIT_HUMAN creates approval bound to the current installation object and is followed by immediate revalidation; DR-09 then yields
568:     EXECUTE_ONCE. A previously granted approval that fails revalidation yields DR-10 INVALIDATED and no submission. Retry is a separate fresh assessment and grants no submission right.
569:   fit_criterion: Every DR-01 through DR-10 branch has a case; identical inputs and policy version produce the same decision. Hard prohibition plus success HIGH, risk LOW, and human Continue
570:     yields BLOCK/BLOCKED with zero backend submissions. COMPLETE, COMPATIBLE, HIGH, LOW, and AUTO_RULES_MET yields ALLOW_AUTO/EXECUTE_ONCE with one submission. HIGH and LOW with AUTO_RULES_NOT_MET
571:     yields REQUIRE_REVIEW/AWAIT_HUMAN. Success not HIGH or risk not LOW yields REQUIRE_REVIEW/AWAIT_HUMAN. Compatibility UNKNOWN or INCOMPATIBLE yields REQUIRE_REVIEW, never ALLOW_AUTO.
572:     KEY_UNKNOWN or TRUNCATED yields RECOLLECT. First Continue creates a fresh binding and revalidates; successful revalidation yields DR-09 EXECUTE_ONCE; changed binding yields DR-10
573:     INVALIDATED with zero submissions. Continue makes zero additional model calls. Preflight rejection yields zero dispatches; reported post-call overage yields one completed call; a
574:     blocked third request yields zero additional dispatches.
575:   source: V0.2 §4.2
576:   depends_on:
577:   - REQ-IX-FR-004
578:   - REQ-IX-SEC-002
579:   status: conceptual
580:   asr: false
581:   enforcing_component: DeterministicPolicyEngine
582:   verification:
583:     method: decision-table + property
584:     test: 'planned: PolicyDecisionTableTest'
585:     evidence: planned
586: - id: REQ-IX-FR-006
587:   type: functional
588:   priority: Must
589:   title: Human review
590:   statement: The system shall display package name, version, signature check, important permissions (dangerous runtime permissions, accessibility, device administration, and install-unknown-apps
591:     related permissions), install_success_likelihood, security_risk, local compatibility result, evidence completeness, AI advice, policy reasons, and any disagreement. For a REQUIRE_REVIEW
592:     request, the first explicit Continue shall create an approval bound to the current installation object under INV-003 and shall then revalidate immediately before submission; no pre-existing
593:     approval is required. Continue shall make zero additional model calls and may submit at most once if revalidation passes. Cancel shall make no submission and shall not reuse an approval.
594:     In RECOLLECT, Continue is disabled and no submittable confirmation is offered. In BLOCK, no continue-install action is offered. Duplicate notification events or repeated Continue
595:     clicks shall not create a second approval or submission. After recovery, an unsubmitted request remains AWAIT_HUMAN until the user acts; a submitted request with an unknown result
596:     shall not be presented as not installed or revocable.
597:   fit_criterion: Before Continue, backend submissions are 0. The first Continue creates an INV-003 binding, revalidates, and, if valid, yields DR-09 EXECUTE_ONCE with one submission
598:     and zero additional model calls. Cancel yields zero submissions. BLOCK has no Continue action. RECOLLECT has disabled confirmation and zero backend calls. Duplicate Continue or notification
599:     replay yields at most one submission. Changed binding yields DR-10 INVALIDATED and zero submissions. After recovery in AWAIT_HUMAN, no auto-approval or submission occurs; after recovery
600:     with unknown submission outcome, RESULT_UNKNOWN is shown and no replay occurs. Disagreement is displayed as consistent, escalated, or downgraded.
601:   source: V0.2 §5.1
602:   depends_on:
603:   - REQ-IX-FR-005
604:   status: conceptual
605:   asr: false
606:   enforcing_component: HumanReviewHandler
607:   verification:
608:     method: UI + negative
609:     test: 'planned: ReviewUiTest'
610:     evidence: planned
611: - id: REQ-IX-FR-007
612:   type: functional
613:   priority: Must
614:   title: Controlled installation
615:   statement: The system shall call the existing installation backend through the single authorized entry point only after ALLOW_AUTO or a valid human approval, and only for an in-scope
616:     AutoDialog or AutoNotification path. Before submission it shall recheck all INV-003 binding fields; if any is missing, changed, or invalidated it shall forbid submission. AutoNotification
617:     shall complete the assessment and decision before submission, shall handle delayed confirmation, process recovery, and duplicate events without creating a new submission right, and
618:     shall not submit more than once per operation. If a prior submission outcome is unknown, automatic replay is forbidden and no new submission may occur until reconciliation resolves
619:     the outcome. Hard prohibitions remain BLOCK.
620:   fit_criterion: Both a valid ALLOW_AUTO and a valid first-Continue approval can reach the test backend; BLOCK, pending review, RECOLLECT, INVALIDATED, and cancelled requests cannot.
621:     If revalidation fails or any binding field is missing or changed, backend submissions are 0. AutoNotification duplicate events and repeated clicks produce at most one submission.
622:     Recovery before submission revalidates and requires user action; recovery after an unknown outcome produces RESULT_UNKNOWN and zero additional submissions or automatic replays. A
623:     hard prohibition produces zero backend submissions even with human approval.
624:   source: V0.2 §4.2
625:   depends_on:
626:   - REQ-IX-FR-005
627:   - REQ-IX-SEC-003
628:   status: conceptual
629:   asr: false
630:   enforcing_component: InstallationGateway
631:   verification:
632:     method: integration + negative
633:     test: 'planned: ControlledInstallTest'
634:     evidence: planned
635: - id: REQ-IX-FR-008
636:   type: functional
637:   priority: Must
638:   title: Feedback and cancellation
639:   statement: The system shall show approval and installation progress and allow cancellation before submission for both in-scope modes; after submission it shall show the platform's
640:     actual status, including RESULT_UNKNOWN, and shall not present an unknown result as not installed or revocable. Delayed notification confirmation shall not submit before assessment
641:     completes.
642:   fit_criterion: Cancelling during model wait, notification delay, or human review results in no submission; cancelling after submission does not label an unknown result as not installed;
643:     status matches the platform check; duplicate notification events produce at most one submission.
644:   source: V0.2 §6 Phase 5
645:   depends_on:
646:   - REQ-IX-FR-001
647:   status: conceptual
648:   asr: false
649:   enforcing_component: InstallerSession UI
650:   verification:
651:     method: UI + negative
652:     test: 'planned: ProgressCancelTest'
653:     evidence: planned
654: - id: REQ-IX-FR-009
655:   type: functional
656:   priority: Must
657:   title: Decision audit
658:   statement: The system shall store, per operation ID and attempt ID, an evidence summary, APK hash, install mode and backend, config and policy versions, model and prompt versions,
659:     install_success_likelihood, security_risk, local compatibility result, evidence completeness, advice or failure type, rule ID, final decision, human action, timestamps, attempt count,
660:     provider-dispatch count, token outcome, and installation result; it shall not store credentials.
661:   fit_criterion: Normal, BLOCK, human-approved, preflight-rejected, post-call-overage, and model-failure records can reconstruct the decision basis; attempts and provider dispatches
662:     are distinguishable; audit contains no tokens or credentials; records are append-only.
663:   source: V0.2 §3.3
664:   depends_on:
665:   - REQ-IX-FR-005
666:   - REQ-IX-REL-002
667:   status: conceptual
668:   asr: false
669:   enforcing_component: DecisionAuditRecorder
670:   verification:
671:     method: audit replay
672:     test: 'planned: AuditRecordTest'
673:     evidence: planned
674: - id: REQ-IX-FR-010
675:   type: functional
676:   priority: Should
677:   title: Query audit
678:   statement: "The user shall be able to view approval records in the app by request, including the final rule, human action, and installation result, and export them in a machine-readable format."
679:   fit_criterion: "Records for two different requests are not mixed; export contains all FR-009 fields; unauthorized users cannot read them."
680:   source: V0.2 §3.3
681:   depends_on:
682:   - REQ-IX-FR-009
683:   status: conceptual
684:   asr: false
685:   enforcing_component: AuditQuery UI
686:   verification:
687:     method: UI + export
688:     test: "planned: AuditQueryTest"
689:     evidence: planned
690: - id: REQ-IX-FR-011
691:   type: functional
692:   priority: Must
693:   title: Outbound data consent
694:   statement: "Before the first transmission to an external model, the system shall display the recipient, the enumerated field list from outbound_metadata_allowlist, purpose, and retention method and obtain explicit consent; after refusal or withdrawal it shall make no model calls, shall not auto-approve, and shall route to REQUIRE_REVIEW (hard prohibitions remain BLOCK); this path is not the same as turning AI off."
695:   fit_criterion: "The consent screen appears on first use; after consent, the request contains only allowlisted fields; after refusal or withdrawal, model calls are 0 and the decision is REQUIRE_REVIEW; separate acceptance cases exist for FR-012 (AI disabled equals baseline); consent and withdrawal are written to audit."
696:   source: V0.2 §9 + privacy risk
697:   depends_on: []
698:   status: conceptual
699:   asr: false
700:   enforcing_component: ConsentGate
701:   verification:
702:     method: UI + counter
703:     test: "planned: ConsentGateTest"
704:     evidence: planned
705: - id: REQ-IX-FR-012
706:   type: functional
707:   priority: Must
708:   title: AI toggle semantics
709:   statement: "When the AI approval switch is off, the system shall preserve existing installation behavior, make no model calls, and record AI_DISABLED in audit; the switch shall not weaken existing signature, blacklist, permission, or policy checks."
710:   fit_criterion: "When off, model calls are 0, existing checks still run, and audit contains AI_DISABLED; this path and the FR-011 consent-declined path are tested separately; under any switch combination, the existing-check pass rate matches baseline."
711:   source: OI-07 (this revision's decision)
712:   depends_on:
713:   - REQ-IX-FR-011
714:   status: conceptual
715:   asr: false
716:   enforcing_component: Settings + ConsentGate
717:   verification:
718:     method: config matrix + negative
719:     test: "planned: ToggleSemanticsTest"
720:     evidence: planned
721: - id: REQ-IX-INV-001
722:   type: invariant
723:   priority: Must
724:   title: AI has no direct privileged execution capability
725:   statement: The AI component shall only return advisory data and shall not hold or call installation, uninstallation, Root, Shizuku, or any installation-backend capability.
726:   fit_criterion: 'Static check: the AI adapter package does not reference InstallationGateway or AppInstallerRepository; dynamic: a model stub returning install or approve instructions
727:     triggers 0 backend calls; both advisory dimensions remain advisory.'
728:   source: V0.2 INV-001
729:   depends_on: []
730:   status: conceptual
731:   asr: false
732:   enforcing_component: ApprovalCoordinator
733:   verification:
734:     method: static + dynamic negative
735:     test: 'planned: AdvisorIsolationTest'
736:     evidence: planned
737: - id: REQ-IX-INV-002
738:   type: invariant
739:   priority: Must
740:   title: Advice does not override deterministic prohibition
741:   statement: Neither AI advice nor human confirmation shall override an active hard-prohibition rule; signature anomalies, blacklist, forbidden downgrade, test-only, and similar rules
742:     are enforced by deterministic code. A high success likelihood or low risk assessment does not change a hard-prohibition result.
743:   fit_criterion: When AI returns HIGH success and LOW risk and the user confirms, a prohibited APK remains BLOCK; backend calls are 0; with AI disabled the same rule still yields BLOCK.
744:   source: V0.2 INV-002
745:   depends_on: []
746:   status: conceptual
747:   asr: false
748:   enforcing_component: DeterministicPolicyEngine
749:   verification:
750:     method: negative
751:     test: 'planned: HardBlockPrecedenceTest'
752:     evidence: planned
753: - id: REQ-IX-INV-003
754:   type: invariant
755:   priority: Must
756:   title: Approval binds the installation object
757:   statement: An approval shall bind operation ID, attempt ID, APK SHA-256, package name, target user, install mode, installation backend, config snapshot, and policy version; if any
758:     binding item is missing or changed the approval becomes invalid and shall be revalidated before submission. The first Continue in AWAIT_HUMAN creates this binding from the current
759:     installation object.
760:   fit_criterion: Changing any binding field invalidates the old approval; a replacement between evidence read and submission cannot install unapproved bytes; first Continue creates a
761:     binding and revalidation pass rate is 100%.
762:   source: V0.2 INV-003
763:   depends_on:
764:   - REQ-IX-FR-002
765:   status: conceptual
766:   asr: true
767:   asr_rationale: Determines the approval state model, execution boundary, and pre-submission revalidation; it is a core structural constraint of the safety chain.
768:   enforcing_component: ApprovalStateStore
769:   verification:
770:     method: negative + TOCTOU
771:     test: 'planned: ApprovalBindingTest'
772:     evidence: planned
773:   note: The target package name remains local and is retained in this binding; see outbound_metadata_allowlist.local_approval_binding.
774: - id: REQ-IX-INV-004
775:   type: invariant
776:   priority: Must
777:   title: Model failure does not silently approve
778:   statement: On model timeout, network loss, rate limiting, service error, invalid output, preflight token rejection, or reported post-call overage, the system shall not auto-approve;
```

````
24: `grep` confirms **no** `ApprovalCoordinator`, `InstallationGateway`, `ApprovalBinding`, or `ApprovalStateStore` exists in `app/src/main`. The blueprint §3.2 lists exactly these as the missing downstream work. This plan is that work's first slice.

26: **Authoritative types we must consume, not redefine**, from `domain/engine/policy/PolicyDecisionModels.kt`:
27: `EvaluatedPolicy`, `HumanApprovalState`, `PolicyAdvice`, `PolicyInput`, `PolicyDecision` (enum), `PolicyDisposition` (enum), `PolicyResult`.
28: 
29: **The hard constraint this plan centers on:** `DeterministicPolicyEngine.evaluate()` returns `EXECUTE_ONCE` but *performs no submission* (`PolicyResult` KDoc, FR-005). DR-09 produces `REQUIRE_REVIEW/EXECUTE_ONCE` only when the caller passes `HumanApprovalState.VALID_APPROVAL_AND_REVALIDATION_PASSED`. Therefore the coordinator must **create the binding, revalidate it, prove revalidation, then submit exactly once** — in that order. A caller that fabricates `VALID_APPROVAL_AND_REVALIDATION_PASSED` without a real revalidation would violate INV-003; the coordinator must be the only place that maps a passed revalidation to that enum value.

87: ### 2.2 ApprovalBinding — the bound installation object (REQ-IX-INV-003)
88: 
89: Fields are **exactly** `outbound_metadata_allowlist.local_approval_binding.retains` in `requirements.yaml` (lines 372–384) and `memory-design.md` §2:
90: 
91: ```kotlin
92: /**
93:  * Implements: ADR-002.7
94:  * Enforces: REQ-IX-INV-003, REQ-IX-SEC-003
95:  */
96: data class ApprovalBinding(
97:     val operationId: String,        // operation_id
98:     val attemptId: String,          // attempt_id
99:     val apkSha256: String,          // apk_sha256 (hex, 64 chars; non-null)
100:     val targetPackageName: String,  // target_package_name (local only, PMA-OUT-001)
101:     val targetUserId: Int,          // target_user_id
102:     val installMode: InstallModeSignal,        // AutoDialog | AutoNotification
103:     val installationBackend: Authorizer,       // backend enum (reused), non-nullable; v1 = None
104:     val configSnapshotHash: String, // config_snapshot (normalized hash, caller-supplied)
105:     val policyVersion: String,      // policy_version
106: )
107: ```
108: 
109: Design decisions (confirmed):
110: - **Q1 — backend (confirmed):** `installationBackend` reuses the existing `com.rosan.installer.domain.settings.model.config.Authorizer` (v1 = `None`) rather than a new enum, to avoid a parallel backend vocabulary. The field is **non-nullable**: a missing backend prevents dispatch, never defaults.
111: - **Q2 — config snapshot (confirmed):** `configSnapshotHash` is a caller-supplied, normalized canonical hash string in this slice. No baseline `ConfigModel` serializer is introduced here; the real canonicalization is a §9 follow-up.
112: - **Q3 — binding construction (confirmed):** `ApprovalBinding` is non-null-only and built by a builder that returns `null` on any missing field, so "a missing binding field prevents dispatch" is structural rather than a silent default.
113: - Equality is structural (`data class`); revalidation compares a freshly constructed binding against the stored one field by field and reports the first mismatch.
114: 
115: ### 2.3 InstallationGateway — single authorized seam (REQ-IX-FR-007, ARCH-001)
116: 
117: ```kotlin
118: /**
119:  * Implements: ADR-002.6
120:  * Enforces: REQ-IX-FR-007, REQ-IX-ARCH-001
121:  */
122: interface InstallationGateway {
123:     /**
124:      * Submits [binding]'s installation object exactly once. The gateway trusts
125:      * only that the coordinator already performed pre-submission revalidation;
126:      * it performs no AI/policy work and holds no model or network capability.
127:      */
128:     suspend fun submit(binding: ApprovalBinding): GatewayResult
129: }
130: 
131: sealed interface GatewayResult {
132:     data object Submitted : GatewayResult                 // backend accepted
133:     data class Failed(val reason: String) : GatewayResult  // backend reported failure
134:     data object ResultUnknown : GatewayResult              // submitted, outcome unknown (FR-008/REL-003)
135: }
136: ```
137: 
138: - `FakeInstallationGateway` (data, test-first-slice) appends each `submit` to a list of `ApprovalBinding` for assertions.
139: - **Do not** put retry, model, or policy inside the gateway. It is the *only* interface that may later wrap `session.install(true)`.
140: - Real-implementation seam (deferred wiring, §10): the production `InstallationGateway` will construct `ConfigModel` + `List<InstallEntity>` from the session and call `AppInstallerRepository.doInstallWork` / `InstallerSessionRepository.install(true)` **only** after the coordinator revalidated. The gateway must not be reachable by UI/AI/policy per ARCH-001.
141: 
142: ### 2.4 ApprovalCoordinator — the sequencer (FR-005/006/007)
143: 
144: Inputs: a `PolicyInput` assembled by the caller (evidence completeness, compatibility, advice from `RequestInstallRiskAssessmentUseCase`, `EvaluatedPolicy`, current `HumanApprovalState`), plus a `BindingFactsProvider` that re-reads the current object's facts. The coordinator reads the provider twice on Continue (§2.5) rather than reusing one snapshot.
145: 
146: State model (from `memory-design.md` §1; `RESULT_UNKNOWN` is a post-submission result, **not** a disposition):
147: 
148: ```
149: RECEIVED → AWAITING_AI | RECOLLECT
150: AWAITING_AI → AWAIT_HUMAN | BLOCKED | EXECUTE_ONCE
151: AWAIT_HUMAN --Continue(first)--> [create binding] → revalidate
152:                 revalidate PASS → EXECUTE_ONCE → submit once → SUBMITTED → COMPLETED|RESULT_UNKNOWN
153:                 revalidate FAIL → INVALIDATED (no submission)
154: AWAIT_HUMAN --Cancel--> CANCELLED (no submission)
155: any pre-submission --Cancel--> CANCELLED
156: ```
157: 
158: Public operations (each guarded so a repeated event is a no-op, INV-005):
159: 
160: | Operation | Behavior | Requirements |
161: |---|---|---|
162: | `decide(input, bindingFacts)` | run engine once; route to `AWAIT_HUMAN`/`BLOCKED`/`EXECUTE_ONCE`; persist decision (fake store) | FR-005, INV-004 |
163: | `onContinue()` | if state≠`AWAIT_HUMAN` or Continue disabled ⇒ no-op/reject; read facts once via `BindingFactsProvider`, build binding from them, store; **then re-read current facts via `BindingFactsProvider` again** and compare field by field against the stored binding; if PASS ⇒ engine with `HumanApprovalState.VALID_APPROVAL_AND_REVALIDATION_PASSED` ⇒ DR-09 `EXECUTE_ONCE` ⇒ `ledger.tryAcquire(operationId)` ⇒ gateway.submit(binding) once; if FAIL ⇒ engine with `..._FAILED_AFTER_APPROVAL` ⇒ DR-10 `INVALIDATED`, 0 submissions | FR-005/006, INV-003 |
164: | `onCancel()` | `CANCELLED`; no submission; no approval reuse | FR-006 |
165: | `onModelFailure(code)` | route `PolicyAdvice.Failed/Unusable` ⇒ no submit (DR-08) | INV-004 |
166: | `revalidatedSubmit(binding, provider)` (internal) | the only producer of `VALID_APPROVAL_AND_REVALIDATION_PASSED`; re-reads facts from `provider` and compares to `binding` | INV-003, SEC-003 |
167: | `onRecovered(state)` | R1–R5 recovery: `AWAIT_HUMAN` stays awaited; `EXECUTE_ONCE` unsubmitted ⇒ require user action (no auto-replay); submitted+unknown ⇒ `RESULT_UNKNOWN`; never auto-approve | REL-003 |
168: 
169: The coordinator holds **no** model SDK, network, or backend except the `InstallationGateway` and `BindingFactsProvider` references (permission-model §9.1 allows exactly this). Submission happens **only** via `gateway.submit`, **only** after the binding re-read passes and `ledger.tryAcquire` succeeds. Critically, the coordinator does **not** reuse the first fact snapshot: revalidation must read current facts afresh (§2.5).
170: 
171: ### 2.5 BindingFactsProvider — fresh facts for revalidation (INV-003, TOCTOU)
172: 
173: The apk sha256, config snapshot, target user, package, install mode, backend, and policy version must be re-read from current state **after** the binding is created, immediately before `ledger.tryAcquire` and `gateway.submit`. Reusing the snapshot that built the binding would let an APK replacement or config change between evidence read and submission go undetected (INV-003, ADR-002.7).
174: 
175: ```kotlin
176: /**
177:  * Implements: ADR-002.7
178:  * Enforces: REQ-IX-INV-003, REQ-IX-SEC-003
179:  *
180:  * Re-reads the current installation facts so the coordinator can rebuild an
181:  * ApprovalBinding and compare it field by field to the stored bound object.
182:  * A provider that returns different facts than the stored binding drives
183:  * DR-10 (INVALIDATED) and zero submissions. It holds no AI/policy/backend
184:  * capability; it only observes current local facts.
185:  */
186: interface BindingFactsProvider {
187:     /** Current facts for [operationId]; called at least twice on Continue. */
188:     suspend fun currentFacts(operationId: String): BindingFacts?
189: }
190: 
191: /**
192:  * The raw inputs a [ApprovalBinding] is built from. A null field means "not
193:  * currently known"; the builder maps any null to a null binding (Q3), so a
194:  * missing fact blocks dispatch instead of defaulting.
195:  */
196: data class BindingFacts(
197:     val apkSha256: String?,
198:     val targetPackageName: String?,
199:     val targetUserId: Int?,
200:     val installMode: InstallModeSignal?,
201:     val installationBackend: Authorizer?,
202:     val configSnapshotHash: String?,
203:     val policyVersion: String?,
204: )
205: ```
206: 
207: Revalidation contract: the coordinator calls `currentFacts(operationId)` once to build the binding, then calls it **again** before acquiring the submission permit; it reconstructs a binding from the second read and compares every field (including `apkSha256`, `configSnapshotHash`, `targetUserId`) to the stored binding. Any difference ⇒ DR-10 `INVALIDATED`, 0 submissions. If the second read yields a null (fact no longer known), that is also a mismatch ⇒ `INVALIDATED` (missing field prevents dispatch).
208: 
209: ### 2.6 ApprovalStateStore (REL-002 contract, fail-closed)
210: 
211: 
212: ```kotlin
213: /**
214:  * Implements: ADR-002.3 (contract only; Room impl deferred)
215:  * Enforces: REQ-IX-REL-002
216:  */
217: interface ApprovalStateStore {
218:     /** Returns true iff the write is durable. A false MUST stop automatic submission. */
219:     suspend fun persist(snapshot: ApprovalSnapshot): Boolean
220:     suspend fun load(operationId: String): ApprovalSnapshot?
221: }
222: ```
223: 
224: `ApprovalSnapshot` = `operationId`, `attemptId`, `ApprovalBinding?`, `ApprovalState`, `PolicyResult?`. This slice uses a **test-only** `InMemoryApprovalStateStore` (under `app/src/test/`); a write failure is simulated in tests to prove **no automatic submission** (REL-002 fit criterion). Room table + DAO remain ADR-002.3 (not started).
225: 
226: ### 2.7 SubmissionLedger (INV-005, REL-004)
227: 
228: Single-consume per `operationId`; thread-safe (`Mutex` or synchronized). `tryAcquire(id): Boolean` returns true at most once per id for the lifetime of the configured dedup window. Retry replays call `onContinue` again but `tryAcquire` fails ⇒ no second submission.

323: ## 6. DR-01…DR-10 handling specifically
324: 
325: The engine already implements DR-01…DR-10 (`DeterministicPolicyEngineTest` §… ). The coordinator's job per rule:
326: 
327: | Rule | Coordinator action |
328: |---|---|
329: | DR-01 HARD_BLOCK | even with human approval, `decide`/`onContinue` must not reach gateway. Engine returns BLOCK regardless of `human`; coordinator submits only on `EXECUTE_ONCE`. **Negative test:** hard block + approved + Continue ⇒ 0 submissions. |
330: | DR-10 INVALIDATED | occurred when `onContinue` revalidation (second provider read vs stored binding) fails ⇒ engine `..._FAILED_AFTER_APPROVAL` ⇒ 0 submissions; state INVALIDATED. |
331: | DR-03 RECOLLECT | Continue disabled; `onContinue` rejected; 0 submissions. |
332: | DR-02/04/06/07/08 AWAIT_HUMAN | `onContinue` available; only revalidation pass + DR-09 ⇒ submit. |
333: | DR-05 ALLOW_AUTO | direct `EXECUTE_ONCE` without human; coordinator acquires ledger + submits once. |
334: | **DR-09** | produced **only** by revalidation pass inside `onContinue`; the coordinator is the sole producer of the `VALID_APPROVAL_AND_REVALIDATION_PASSED` input. This is the INV-003 boundary. |
335: 
336: **CRITICAL** — first Continue creates approval then immediately revalidates, then submits per DR-09; this must be one flow. The test `firstContinueBindsRevalidatesAndSubmitsOnce` asserts 1 submission and 0 extra model calls.

348: | Continue after Cancel | state `CANCELLED` ⇒ `onContinue` no-op | `cancelYieldsZeroSubmissions` |

353: ## 8. Persistence, restart, RESULT_UNKNOWN honesty (REL-002/003/004)
354: 
355: - This slice **does not** persist to Room. It provides the `ApprovalStateStore` contract with an explicit **fail-closed** bool and an in-memory impl, plus tests that inject write failure and a simulated restart (load after store reset). This **does not** by itself satisfy REL-002/003/004 for real process death; it proves the *logic and contract*. §10 lists it as an unmet Must gap until Room (ADR-002.3) is built.
````

```
4:
```

```
7: 候选转换接收**同一次分析的 `PackageAnalysisResult`、已明确选中的普通单 APK `BaseEntity`，以及 D1 要求的现有结构化检查结论**，组装现有 `InstallEvidence`。转换只使用内存中的分析结果，不读取 APK、不重做 Android 检查、不触发 Advisor 或安装。不能确认候选归属或输入超出单普通 APK 范围时，按批准的契约拒绝转换或返回明确的不可用结果，不从候选列表任取第一项。

12: | APK 文件摘要 | 使用选中 `BaseEntity.fileHash`，缺失时不填造、不另算，也不拿 `signatureHash` 替代。保留现有 `completeness()` 对缺少文件摘要返回 `UNREADABLE` 的行为。文件摘要不出站。 |
```

```
17:  * Enforces: REQ-IX-MOD-001, REQ-IX-FR-003, REQ-IX-COST-001
18:  *
19:  * Single-provider adapter for the **Groq** OpenAI-compatible chat
20:  * completions API (`https://api.groq.com/openai/v1/chat/completions`).
21:  * One provider only for v1; the [AiModelClient] interface keeps the
22:  * provider replaceable without touching the policy gate (REQ-IX-MOD-001).
23:  *
24:  * A response cut off by the token cap is reported as
25:  * [AiAdvisorFailure.TokenLimitExceeded] rather than being passed on as text,
26:  * so a truncated reply is a failure status and never a partial assessment
27:  * (`runtime-policy-catalog.md` F-08).
28:  */
29: class GroqAiModelClient(
30:     private val transport: OpenAiCompatibleTransport,
31:     override val modelId: String = DEFAULT_MODEL,
32:     private val json: Json = Json,
33: ) : AiModelClient {
34: 
35:     override suspend fun complete(request: AiInstallRiskRequest): String {
36:         val body = OpenAiCompatiblePayload.build(
37:             json = json,
38:             model = modelId,
39:             systemPrompt = request.systemPrompt,
40:             userPrompt = request.userPrompt,
41:             maxOutputTokens = request.maxOutputTokens,
42:             jsonObjectMode = true,
43:         )
44:         val raw = transport.post(path = CHAT_COMPLETIONS_PATH, body = body)
45:         return guardedContent(raw, request.maxOutputTokens)
46:     }
47: 
48:     /**
49:      * Rejects a completion that the provider reports as truncated or
50:      * filtered. If the envelope cannot be read far enough to tell, the raw
51:      * body is returned unchanged and the strict parser reports the failure
52:      * instead (F-05), so there is one honest failure path.
53:      */
54:     internal fun guardedContent(raw: String, maxOutputTokens: Int): String {
55:         val root = runCatching { json.parseToJsonElement(raw) as? JsonObject }.getOrNull()
56:             ?: return raw
57:         val firstChoice = runCatching {
58:             (root["choices"] as JsonArray)[0].jsonObject
59:         }.getOrNull() ?: return raw
60: 
61:         val finishReason = (firstChoice["finish_reason"] as? JsonPrimitive)?.contentOrNull
62:         if (finishReason == null || finishReason == "stop") return raw
63: 
64:         if (finishReason == "content_filter") {
65:             throw AiAdvisorFailure.TokenLimitExceeded("completion blocked by content filter")
66:         }
67:         throw AiAdvisorFailure.TokenLimitExceeded(
68:             "completion truncated after $maxOutputTokens output tokens (finish_reason=$finishReason)",
69:         )
70:     }
71: 
72:     companion object {
73:         const val BASE_URL = "https://api.groq.com/openai/v1"
74:         const val CHAT_COMPLETIONS_PATH = "chat/completions"
75: 
76:         /** Default model; override with [AiModelClient.modelId]. */
77:         const val DEFAULT_MODEL = "qwen/qwen3-32b"
78: 
79:         /** Model tokens and endpoints are never logged (REQ-IX-FR-009). */
80:         const val ENV_API_KEY = "GROQ_API_KEY"
81:     }
82: }
```

```
26: /**
27:  * Implements: ADR-002.2; ADR-002.5
28:  * Enforces: REQ-IX-INV-004, REQ-IX-SEC-004, REQ-IX-FR-009
29:  *
30:  * OkHttp transport for OpenAI-compatible endpoints.
31:  *
32:  * **Network boundary.** It re-checks [egressAllowed] immediately before the
33:  * request leaves the process, so a caller that skips the gate still cannot
34:  * egress while the in-app network setting is off (`AGENTS.md`). It also reads
35:  * the assessment's current consent immediately before dispatch (REQ-IX-FR-012).
36:  * Withdrawal cannot recall an in-flight request.
37:  *
38:  * **Secrets.** The API key is read through a lambda and is never logged,
39:  * stored in the request object, or included in failure messages
40:  * (REQ-IX-FR-009).
41:  *
42:  * **Bounded.** One exchange, a hard read timeout, and a response-size cap;
43:  * no automatic retry (REQ-IX-COST-001).
44:  *
45:  * **Shared stack.** When a base [OkHttpClient] is supplied (the app's
46:  * existing one from `di/NetworkModule.kt`), it is reused through
47:  * `newBuilder()` with only the model-call timeouts overridden, so the
48:  * advisory path adds no second HTTP stack and no new framework.
49:  */
50: class OkHttpAiTransport(
51:     private val baseUrl: String = GroqAiModelClient.BASE_URL,
52:     private val modelId: String = GroqAiModelClient.DEFAULT_MODEL,
53:     private val apiKeyProvider: () -> String?,
54:     private val egressAllowed: suspend () -> Boolean = { true },
55:     baseClient: OkHttpClient? = null,
56:     readTimeoutSeconds: Long = READ_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
57:     private val maxResponseBytes: Int = MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES,
58:     private val json: Json = Json { ignoreUnknownKeys = true },
59: ) : OpenAiCompatibleTransport {
60: 
61:     private val client: OkHttpClient = (
62:         baseClient?.newBuilder()
63:             ?: OkHttpClient.Builder()
64:                 .connectTimeout(CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
65:         )
66:         .readTimeout(readTimeoutSeconds, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
67:         .build()
68: 
69:     override suspend fun post(path: String, body: String): String = withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
70:         if (!egressAllowed()) {
71:             throw AiAdvisorFailure.NetworkDisabled("network egress is disabled in app settings")
72:         }
73: 
74:         val apiKey = readApiKey()
75: 
76:         val request = Request.Builder()
77:             .url("${baseUrl.trimEnd('/')}/$path")
78:             .header("Authorization", "Bearer $apiKey")
79:             .header("Content-Type", "application/json")
80:             .post(body.toRequestBody(JSON_MEDIA_TYPE))
81:             .build()
82: 
83:         if (!ModelRequestGate.hasCurrentConsent()) throw AiAdvisorFailure.ConsentUnavailable()
84: 
85:         try {
86:             client.newCall(request).execute().use { response ->
87:                 when {
88:                     response.code == 429 -> {
89:                         val retryAfter = response.header("Retry-After")?.toLongOrNull()
90:                         throw AiAdvisorFailure.RateLimited(retryAfter)
91:                     }
92: 
93:                     // Preflight token rejection: the request itself is too
94:                     // large for the model. No completion was produced, but a
95:                     // dispatch was consumed (F-07 / F-08).
96:                     response.code == 413 -> {
97:                         throw AiAdvisorFailure.TokenLimitExceeded(
98:                             "request rejected as too large (HTTP 413)",
99:                         )
100:                     }
101: 
102:                     response.code == 400 && isTokenLimitError(response) -> {
103:                         throw AiAdvisorFailure.TokenLimitExceeded(
104:                             "provider rejected the request for exceeding a token limit (HTTP 400)",
105:                         )
106:                     }
107: 
108:                     !response.isSuccessful -> {
109:                         // Response bodies of error replies may echo request data;
110:                         // never log them, keep only the status code.
111:                         throw AiAdvisorFailure.ServiceError(response.code, "HTTP ${response.code}")
112:                     }
113: 
114:                     else -> {
115:                         val source = response.body.source()
116:                         val read = source.readByteArray(maxResponseBytes.toLong() + 1)
117:                         if (read.size > maxResponseBytes) {
118:                             throw AiAdvisorFailure.OutputOversize(read.size, maxResponseBytes)
119:                         }
120:                         extractContent(read.decodeToString(), modelId)
121:                     }
122:                 }
123:             }
124:         } catch (io: InterruptedIOException) {
125:             throw AiAdvisorFailure.Timeout(io.message ?: "request timed out")
126:         } catch (io: IOException) {
127:             throw AiAdvisorFailure.NetworkError(io.message ?: "network error")
128:         }
129:     }
130: 
131:     /** Reads a usable Bearer credential without exposing the key or the source error (REQ-IX-FR-009). */
132:     private fun readApiKey(): String {
133:         val key = try {
134:             apiKeyProvider()
135:         } catch (cancelled: CancellationException) {
136:             throw cancelled
137:         } catch (_: Exception) {
138:             throw AiAdvisorFailure.ApiKeyUnavailable()
139:         }
140:         return key?.takeIf { it.isNotEmpty() && it.all { char -> char in '!'..'~' } }
141:             ?: throw AiAdvisorFailure.ApiKeyUnavailable()
142:     }
143: 
144:     /**
145:      * Detects an OpenAI-compatible token-limit error without logging the body.
146:      * Only the error `code`/`type` fields are inspected, never free text that
147:      * could echo the prompt (REQ-IX-FR-009).
148:      */
149:     private fun isTokenLimitError(response: Response): Boolean = runCatching {
150:         val body = response.body.string()
151:         if (body.length > MAX_ERROR_SCAN_BYTES) return false
152:         val root = json.parseToJsonElement(body) as? JsonObject ?: return false
153:         val error = root["error"] as? JsonObject ?: return false
154:         val markers = listOf("code", "type")
155:         markers.any { key ->
156:             val value = (error[key] as? JsonPrimitive)?.contentOrNull?.lowercase() ?: return@any false
157:             TOKEN_LIMIT_MARKERS.any { value.contains(it) }
158:         }
159:     }.getOrDefault(false)

161:     /**

165:     internal fun extractContent(raw: String, expectedModelId: String): String {
166:         val root = runCatching { json.parseToJsonElement(raw) as? JsonObject }.getOrNull()

169:         if (reportedModel != null && reportedModel != expectedModelId) {

171:         }
172:         val content = runCatching {
173:             root["choices"]!!.jsonArray[0].jsonObject["message"]!!.jsonObject["content"]!!.jsonPrimitive.content
174:         }.getOrNull() ?: throw AiAdvisorFailure.InvalidOutput("response has no choices[0].message.content")
175:         if (content.isBlank()) {
176:             throw AiAdvisorFailure.InvalidOutput("assistant content is empty")
177:         }
178:         return content
179:     }
180: 
181:     companion object {
182:         const val MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES = 64 * 1024
183:         private const val CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 10L
184: 
185:         /** Error bodies are only scanned for a code; never logged. */
186:         private const val MAX_ERROR_SCAN_BYTES = 8 * 1024
187: 
188:         private val TOKEN_LIMIT_MARKERS = listOf(
189:             "context_length",
190:             "too_large",
191:             "too_many_tokens",
192:             "max_tokens",
193:             "token_limit",
194:             "request_too_large",
195:             "string_above_max_length",
```

```
11: /**

13:  * Enforces: REQ-IX-FR-011, REQ-IX-FR-012, REQ-IX-SEC-004, REQ-IX-INV-004
14:  *
15:  * The caller installs this element with `withContext` around one assessment.
16:  * [readConsent] must read the current authorization for that assessment on
17:  * each check. Only `true` authorizes egress; missing, declined, withdrawn,
18:  * and unreadable consent all deny it. Never supply a cached grant.
19:  */
20: class ModelRequestGate(
21:     private val readConsent: suspend () -> Boolean?,
22: ) : AbstractCoroutineContextElement(Key) {
23:     companion object Key : CoroutineContext.Key<ModelRequestGate> {
24:         /** Reads the current assessment's consent without exposing read failures (REQ-IX-FR-009). */
25:         internal suspend fun hasCurrentConsent(): Boolean {
26:             val context = currentCoroutineContext()
27:             context.ensureActive()
28:             val granted = try {
29:                 context[Key]?.readConsent() == true
```

```
9: /**
10:  * Implements: ADR-001; ADR-002.2
11:  * Enforces: REQ-IX-MOD-001, REQ-IX-INV-001, REQ-IX-QUAL-001, REQ-IX-SEC-001
12:  *
13:  * The advisory boundary. Implementations may reach the model service and
14:  * nothing else: no installer backend, no privileged provider, no session
15:  * repository, no `ActionHandler` (`permission-model.md` section 9.2).
16:  *
17:  * The return type cannot express an install decision, so a model response
18:  * cannot approve anything (REQ-IX-INV-001).
19:  */
20: interface AIRiskAdvisor {
21:     /**
22:      * Performs at most **one** provider dispatch for [request]. No
23:      * automatic retry (REQ-IX-COST-001).
24:      *
25:      * @param knownEvidencePaths the `evidence.*` paths [request] actually
26:      *   carries, as reported by `AiRequestBuilder`. The implementation
27:      *   rejects a citation outside this set as fabricated
28:      *   (REQ-IX-QUAL-001). It is a parameter rather than something the
29:      *   implementation derives, so the advisor never needs to re-parse the
30:      *   payload it was handed.
31:      */
32:     suspend fun assessRequest(
33:         request: AiInstallRiskRequest,
34:         knownEvidencePaths: Set<String>,
35:     ): AdvisorOutcome
36: }
37: 
38: /**
39:  * Implements: ADR-001; ADR-002.2
40:  * Enforces: REQ-IX-FR-003, REQ-IX-MOD-001
41:  *
42:  * Model-service adapter. One implementation per provider; the advisor
43:  * depends only on this interface so the provider is replaceable without
44:  * touching the policy gate (REQ-IX-MOD-001).
45:  */
46: interface AiModelClient {
47:     val modelId: String
48: 
49:     /**
50:      * Sends [request] once and returns the raw response body text.
51:      * Throws [com.rosan.installer.domain.ai.model.AiAdvisorFailure] on
52:      * transport, HTTP, or size failures.
53:      */
54:     suspend fun complete(request: AiInstallRiskRequest): String
55: }
56: 
57: /**

59:  * Enforces: REQ-IX-SEC-004
60:  *
61:  * Egress gate. Never call the model when this returns `false`
62:  * (`AGENTS.md`: network requests stay disabled when the in-app setting
63:  * is off). An implementation must fail closed: an unreadable preference
64:  * means "not allowed", never "allowed by default".
65:  */
66: interface AiNetworkGate {
```

```
10: /**

12:  * Enforces: REQ-IX-SEC-004
13:  *
14:  * Gates model egress on the existing in-app network switch, exactly as
15:  * `OkHttpNetworkResolver.resolve` and `SourceResolver` do
16:  * (`AppPreferences.allowInternetAccess`). No new setting is introduced and
17:  * the baseline network boundary is not widened (`AGENTS.md` critical
18:  * constraints).
19:  *
20:  * **Fails closed.** If the stored setting cannot be read, egress is denied.
21:  * The caller (`DefaultAiRiskAdvisor`) also treats a thrown gate error as
22:  * "network disabled", but that is a second line of defence, not the rule:
23:  * an AI call must never be the one thing that decides it is allowed to
24:  * leave the device when the user's preference is unknown.
25:  */
26: class AppSettingsNetworkGate(
27:     private val appSettingsRepository: AppSettingsRepository,
28: ) : AiNetworkGate {
29:     override suspend fun isEgressAllowed(): Boolean = try {
30:         appSettingsRepository.preferencesFlow.first().allowInternetAccess
31:     } catch (cancelled: CancellationException) {
32:         throw cancelled
33:     } catch (t: Throwable) {
34:         // Unknown preference is not consent: deny.
35:         false
36:     }
37: }
```

```
20: /**
21:  * Implements: ADR-001; ADR-002.2
22:  * Enforces: REQ-IX-FR-003, REQ-IX-SEC-004, REQ-IX-SEC-005
23:  *
24:  * Converts local [InstallEvidence] (APK facts + device compatibility facts)
25:  * into an [AiInstallRiskRequest].
26:  *
27:  * The **allowlist is the single source of truth** and is enforced here by
28:  * construction: only the fields named in [ALLOWLISTED_LEAF_PATHS] are ever
29:  * written into the payload. Local-only values (target package name, APK
30:  * SHA-256, the raw device API level) are used solely for redaction and are
31:  * never serialized (PMA-OUT-001, NFC-OUT-006).
32:  *
33:  * The five installation-context fields (`install_mode`, `target_user_scope`,
34:  * `package_source`, `source_confidence`, `installer_capability`) always carry
35:  * a value key, using the `unknown_encoding` documented in
36:  * `requirements.yaml` where the evidence is unknown.
37:  */
38: class AiRequestBuilder(
39:     private val sanitizer: EvidenceSanitizer = EvidenceSanitizer(),
40:     private val json: Json = Json,
41: ) {
42:     fun build(evidence: InstallEvidence, installedVersionCode: Long? = null): PreparedAiRequest {
43:         val versionNameSanitized = sanitizer.sanitizeField(evidence.versionName)
44:         val versionName = sanitizer.redactLocalIdentifiers(
45:             versionNameSanitized.text,
46:             localIdentifiers(evidence),
47:         )
48:         val (permissions, permissionsTruncated) =
49:             sanitizer.sanitizeList(evidence.declaredPermissions, EvidenceSanitizer.MAX_LIST_ITEMS)
50: 
51:         val payload = buildJsonObject {
52:             evidence.versionCode?.let { put("version_code", it) }
53:             if (versionName.isNotEmpty()) put("version_name", versionName)
54:             evidence.minSdk?.let { put("min_sdk", it) }
55:             evidence.targetSdk?.let { put("target_sdk", it) }
56:             put("declared_permissions", JsonArray(permissions.map(::JsonPrimitive)))
57:             evidence.signatureVerificationStatus?.let {
58:                 put("signature_verification_status", it.name)
59:             }
60:             evidence.installedSignatureMatch?.let { put("installed_signature_match", it.name) }
61:             evidence.installRelation?.let { put("install_relation", it.name) }
62:             evidence.apkIdentity?.let { put("apk_identity", it.name) }
63:             evidence.hasSharedUid?.let { put("has_shared_uid", it) }
64:             evidence.isXposedModule?.let { put("is_xposed_module", it) }
65:             evidence.platformCompatibility?.let { put("platform_compatibility", it.name) }
66:             evidence.abiCompatibility?.let { put("abi_compatibility", it.name) }
67:             evidence.storageSufficient?.let { put("storage_sufficient", it) }
68:             // rev.6 gives no unknown encoding for install_mode, so an unknown
69:             // context is omitted rather than invented.
70:             evidence.installMode?.let { put("install_mode", it.name) }
71:             put("target_user_scope", (evidence.targetUserScope ?: TargetUserScope.UNKNOWN).name)
72:             put("package_source", (evidence.packageSource ?: PackageSourceSignal.UNSPECIFIED).name)
73:             put("source_confidence", (evidence.sourceConfidence ?: SourceConfidenceSignal.UNKNOWN).name)
74:             put(
75:                 "installer_capability",
76:                 (evidence.installerCapability ?: InstallerCapability.UNKNOWN).name,
77:             )
78:         }
79: 
80:         val completeness = evidence.completeness(
81:             truncated = permissionsTruncated || versionNameSanitized.truncated ||
82:                 versionName.length > EvidenceSanitizer.MAX_FIELD_CHARS,
83:         )
84:         val payloadText = json.encodeToString(JsonObject.serializer(), payload)
85: 
86:         return PreparedAiRequest(
87:             request = AiInstallRiskRequest(
88:                 modelId = DEFAULT_MODEL_ID,
89:                 promptVersion = PROMPT_VERSION,
90:                 systemPrompt = SYSTEM_PROMPT,
91:                 userPrompt = userPrompt(payloadText, completeness, evidence, installedVersionCode, permissions.size),
92:                 evidencePayloadJson = payloadText,
93:                 maxOutputTokens = MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS,
94:             ),
95:             completeness = completeness,
96:             transmittedPaths = payload.keys.mapTo(linkedSetOf()) { "evidence.$it" },
97:         )
98:     }
99: 
100:     private fun localIdentifiers(evidence: InstallEvidence): List<String> = listOfNotNull(evidence.targetPackageName)
101: 
102:     private fun userPrompt(
103:         payloadText: String,
104:         completeness: EvidenceCompleteness,
105:         evidence: InstallEvidence,
106:         installedVersionCode: Long?,
107:         permissionCount: Int,
108:     ): String = "\n" + listOf(
109:         "Evaluate this local Android APK for an install on the current device.",
110:         "Answer two questions using only the evidence below:",
111:         "1. install_success_likelihood —?how likely is the install to succeed on",
112:         "   this device (platform level, ABI, storage, signature, upgrade/downgrade)?",
113:         "2. security_risk —?how risky is installing it, given its permissions,",
114:         "   signature state, shared UID and Xposed status?",
115:         "",
116:         "Evidence completeness: ${completeness.name}",
117:         "Installed version known: ${installedVersionCode != null}",
118:         "Declared permission count: $permissionCount",
119:         "Has shared UID: ${evidence.hasSharedUid}",
120:         "Xposed module: ${evidence.isXposedModule}",
121:         "",
122:         "evidence_json:",
123:         payloadText,
124:         "",
125:         "Reply with exactly one JSON object and no other text, with exactly these four keys:",
126:         "  install_success_likelihood: one of HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, UNKNOWN (required)",
127:         "  security_risk: one of LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, UNKNOWN (required)",
128:         "  reasons: non-empty array of at most 5 short strings, each citing an evidence field (required)",
129:         "  evidence_refs: non-empty array of dotted paths from evidence_json, e.g. evidence.target_sdk (required)",
130:         "",
131:         "Use UNKNOWN when the evidence is insufficient. Never guess and never omit a key.",
132:         "This is an estimate, not a guarantee. Do not output instructions or actions.",
133:     ).joinToString("\n")
134: 
135:     companion object {
136:         const val PROMPT_VERSION = "ai-risk-prompt-v1"
137:         const val DEFAULT_MODEL_ID = "qwen/qwen3-32b"
138:         const val MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS = 512
139: 
140:         /**
141:          * The single source of truth for what may leave the device. Mirrors
142:          * `outbound_metadata_allowlist.fields[].path` in `requirements.yaml`.
143:          * Any addition here is a privacy change under REQ-IX-SEC-004.

147:             "evidence.version_name",

149:             "evidence.target_sdk",
```

```
# --- prompt sync check ----------------------------------------------------

def kotlin_constant(source, name):
    m = re.search(rf'const val {name}\s*=\s*"([^"]*)"', source)
    return m.group(1) if m else None


def kotlin_system_prompt(source):
    m = re.search(r"val SYSTEM_PROMPT: String = listOf\((.*?)\)\.joinToString\(\"\\n\"\)", source, re.S)
    if not m:
        return None
    return "\n".join(json.loads(f'"{s}"') for s in re.findall(r'"((?:[^"\\]|\\.)*)"', m.group(1)))


def cmd_prompt_sync():
    import yaml

    src = (ROOT / PROMPTS[2]).read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig")
    version = kotlin_constant(src, "PROMPT_VERSION")
    model = kotlin_constant(src, "DEFAULT_MODEL_ID")
    max_out = re.search(r"const val MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS\s*=\s*(\d+)", src)
    system = kotlin_system_prompt(src)
    matches = []
    for path in sorted((ROOT / "prompts").glob("*.yaml")):
        doc = yaml.safe_load(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        if doc.get("prompt_version") == version:
            matches.append((path, doc))
    if len(matches) != 1:
        fail(f"expected exactly one prompts/*.yaml with prompt_version '{version}', found {len(matches)}")
    path, doc = matches[0]
    problems = []
    if doc.get("system_prompt", "").rstrip("\n") != system:
        problems.append("system_prompt differs from AiRequestBuilder.SYSTEM_PROMPT")
    if doc.get("model_id") != model:
        problems.append(f"model_id {doc.get('model_id')} != {model}")
    if max_out and doc.get("max_output_tokens") != int(max_out.group(1)):
        problems.append(f"max_output_tokens {doc.get('max_output_tokens')} != {max_out.group(1)}")
    for p in problems:
        print(f"  {p}")
    if problems:
        fail(f"{path.relative_to(ROOT)} is out of sync with the code; bump the version for any prompt change")
    print(f"prompt sync passed: {path.relative_to(ROOT)} matches prompt version {version}")


COMMANDS = {
    "schema": (cmd_schema, 0),
    "changes": (cmd_changes, 2),
    "ai-use-log": (cmd_ai_use_log, 2),
    "test-approval": (cmd_test_approval, 2),
    "permissions": (cmd_permissions, 0),
    "dependencies": (cmd_dependencies, 0),
    "prompt-sync": (cmd_prompt_sync, 0),
}

if __name__ == "__main__":
    if len(sys.argv) < 2 or sys.argv[1] not in COMMANDS:
        print(__doc__)
        sys.exit(2)
    fn, nargs = COMMANDS[sys.argv[1]]
    if len(sys.argv) - 2 != nargs:
        print(__doc__)
```

```
24:  * **Not** part of the deterministic offline suite

32:  * a key stays green.

34:  * What it asserts is deliberately narrow, because a live model's *judgement*
35:  * is not stable and must not be asserted:
36:  *
37:  * - every scenario produces either a fully-formed assessment or an explicit
38:  *   failure status — never a crash and never a partial object;
39:  * - each scenario costs at most one dispatch;
40:  * - if the model did answer usefully, its citations are real;
41:  * - a live transport failure is reported as a classified failure, not a

46: class GroqLiveAdvisorTest {

72:                 outputValidator = StrictAiOutputValidator(),
73:             ),

77:         val failures = mutableListOf<String>()

79:         for (scenario in EvidenceFixtures.all) {

81:             println(

83:                     "dispatches=${status.providerDispatches} " +

85:                     "assessment=${status.assessment?.assessment}",
```

```
273: @Composable
274: private fun NetworkSourceModeWidget(currentMode: NetworkSourceMode, onModeChange: (NetworkSourceMode) -> Unit) {
275:     val modes = linkedMapOf(
276:         NetworkSourceMode.Cache to stringResource(R.string.config_network_source_cache),
277:         NetworkSourceMode.Smart to stringResource(R.string.config_network_source_smart),
278:         NetworkSourceMode.LowStorage to stringResource(R.string.config_network_source_low_storage),
279:     )
280:     val descriptions = mapOf(
281:         NetworkSourceMode.Cache to stringResource(R.string.config_network_source_cache_desc),
282:         NetworkSourceMode.Smart to stringResource(R.string.config_network_source_smart_desc),
283:         NetworkSourceMode.LowStorage to stringResource(R.string.config_network_source_low_storage_desc),
284:     )
285: 
286:     DropDownMenuWidget(
287:         icon = AppIcons.NetworkSource,
288:         title = stringResource(R.string.config_network_source_mode),
289:         description = descriptions.getValue(currentMode),
290:         choice = modes.keys.indexOf(currentMode).coerceAtLeast(0),
291:         data = modes.values.toList(),
292:         onChoiceChange = { index ->
293:             modes.keys.elementAtOrNull(index)?.let(onModeChange)
294:         },
295:     )
296: }

303:             HttpProfile.ALLOW_LOCAL,
304:             HttpProfile.ALLOW_ALL,
305:         )

307:     val options = profiles.map { profile ->
```
